title: The Computational Anatomy of Humility: Modeling Intellectual Humility in Online Public Discourse

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4 ('To ensure determinism in the generated responses, we set the temperature parameter of the LLMs to zero'); max_tokens assumed (a single class name)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: the 194 of 350 screened Reddit posts that received at least one code from the final codebook; each carries a composite IH / IA / Neutral label inferred from the individual codes
task.approximation: the released data.csv is the full 1,412-post screening pool with in-progress per-annotator labels, not the cleaned 350/194-post gold standard, so the evaluation set cannot be cut exactly

items.source: https://github.com/xiaobo-guo/The-Computational-Anatomy-of-Humility-Modeling-Intellectual-Humility-in-Online-Public-Discourse, file data.csv (3.26 MB, 1,412 rows) - the link is a PDF hyperlink on page 1 ('Our dataset is available at Dataset') whose target is lost in the text extraction and was recovered from the link annotations of aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.327.pdf
items.config_or_split: single csv; Reddit threads from 48 religion-oriented subreddits
items.column_counts: 1,412 rows; annotator Neil labelled 456, annotator Melody 268, union 503; 'final_labels' is filled for only 21 rows; 'done_coding?' is 'No' on every row
items.filter_paper: rows whose final composite IH/IA/Neutral label is defined - not expressible against the released columns (see open points)

prompt.system:
You are a classifier for predicting whether the given text is intellectual humility, intellectual arrogant, or neutral. You must choose the answer from the following options: neutral, intellectual humility, and intellectual arrogance.
Intellectual humility means recognizing that their beliefs might be wrong, including the following features: {IH_code}. If it follows any of this, it should be labeled as Intellectual humility.
Intellectual arrogance is a state of mind where someone has an exaggerated view of their own intellect and knowledge and believes it is superior to others, such as the following features: {IA_code}. The list of features is not exhaustive.
Neutral means not related to religious discourse or not enough information to classify as intellectual humility or intellectual arrogance.
prompt.user_template:
Here is a discussion with the title: '{Post_title}', and the content is as follows: '{Post_content}'. The first comment is: '{First_comment}'.

The second comment is: '{Second_comment}'.

Based on the content do you think Comment: '{Focal_comment}' is '{Label}' or not.

placeholders.IH_code: the IH half of the final codebook (Table 2) as name + description pairs - Code-and-Description setting
placeholders.IA_code: the IA half of the final codebook (Table 2) as name + description pairs
placeholders.Second_comment: items.comment_2 (only when the focal post is the second comment)
placeholders.Label: the class being asked about

prompt.few_shot: none (the Few-shot and CoT variants of Appendix C.2 are separate, later experiments)
prompt.source_location: Appendix C.1.1 (IH/IA/Neutral system prompt, Code-and-Description variant) and C.1.3 (user prompt, identical for all tasks and settings)
prompt.verbatim: partial - the text is Appendix C.1 as printed, with the spacing damage of the monospace listing repaired (the extraction inserts a space before every comma and inside every brace pair, e.g. 'intellectual humility ,' -> 'intellectual humility,' and '{ { IH_code } }' -> '{IH_code}') and the Guidance wrappers ({{#system~}} ... {{~/system}}, the {{#if focus_on_second_comment}} block) resolved into plain message content. The printed user prompt carries a {Label} slot that belongs to the label-wise Binary-Question task; no separate user prompt is printed for the three-way IH/IA/Neutral task.

output.parse: label from set [neutral, intellectual humility, intellectual arrogance]
output.parse_paper: unstated; the paper only says the prompts were iteratively refined 'to ensure the generated text adhered closely to the instructions'

metric.name: macro_f1
metric.definition: Macro-F1 of the three-way IH / IA / Neutral prediction against the human gold label, averaged over the two annotators' reference sets (Sec. 4.1: 'The F1 score reported is an average derived from comparing the labels generated by two annotators on a subset of samples and labels')
metric.original_location: Table 3, IH/IA/NE column, C&D block, GPT-4 row (0.70). In Table 3 the IH/IA/NE value spans the BQ and MS rows of a content variation, because Sec. 4.2 states that the three-way task 'is impossible to format into BQ; therefore, we only test with MS' - so the 0.70 cell is the Code-and-Description content with the Multiple-Selection format.

open_points: gold labels: the released data.csv is the raw screening pool. 'done_coding?' is 'No' on all 1,412 rows, 'final_labels' is filled on 21, and the two annotator columns cover 456 and 268 rows (union 503) - none of these equals the 350 screened or the 194 labelled posts of the paper, so the evaluation set and its IH/IA/Neutral gold cannot be cut without a decision about which column and which subset the authors used.

codebook: the {IH_code} and {IA_code} slots have to be filled with the final codebook of Table 2 (label name + description + whether the label is IH or IA). Table 2 survives the PDF extraction only in fragments (two of about a dozen rows), so the prompt cannot be completed from the text at hand.

prompt slot: Appendix C.1.3 prints one user prompt for all settings, ending in "is '{Label}' or not", which fits the binary per-code task rather than the three-way IH/IA/Neutral classification the 0.70 cell reports; how the three-way question was posed is not printed.

metric definition: 'an average derived from comparing the labels generated by two annotators on a subset of samples and labels' leaves the averaging unit (per annotator, per label, per sample) undetermined.
notes: Recovered link (2026-09-19): the page-1 footnote 'Our dataset is available at Dataset' points at github.com/xiaobo-guo/The-Computational-Anatomy-of-Humility-... ; the repository holds README.md and data.csv only. GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 is evaluated beside GPT-4 in the same table and is out of scope.
